title: “Pull or Not to Pull?”: Investigating Moral Biases in Leading Large Language Models Across Ethical Dilemmas

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM intervention decisions and natural language justifications across 27 variations of the trolley problem, framed by 10 distinct moral philosophies, to measure ethical alignment, assertiveness, and divergence from human consensus.

Measuring contextual response asymmetries in trolley problem scenarios involving different animals (e.g., sacrificing a cat vs. five lobsters) to reveal latent biases in how models weigh species and sentience.
Analyzing intervention rates in dilemmas involving relational proximity, specifically testing if a model changes its moral decision when the scenario involves saving a best friend versus strangers.
Testing the influence of financial incentives on ethical decision-making by introducing a scenario where the model is offered a $1,000,000 bribe to pull the lever.
